title: Register Nuance: Integrating Vernacular Particles vs. Elevated B2 Discourse

sections.title: Agglutinative Assimilation of Digital Neologisms
sections.content: Hungarian absorbs English loanwords by integrating them into its productive derivational and inflectional matrix. Stems adopt the suffix '-ol/-el/-öl' to form verbs, accept verbal prefixes (elposztol, kilájkol), and conform strictly to vowel harmony (e.g. stalkol -> stalkoltam, stalkolás).

sections.title: Managing Register Boundaries in Professional and Academic Life
sections.content: Advanced communicative competence hinges on code-switching. Using informal discourse particles (ugye, hát, izé) or internet neologisms (lájkol, krindzs) creates rapport among peers, but produces jarring register clashes in formal interviews, official correspondence, and academic essays.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: To achieve B2/C1 mastery, observe where native speakers employ youth vernacular versus formal phrasing. Never mix colloquial internet abbreviations with formal passive or participial constructions.
